item.title: Gold climbs as Middle East conflict and weaker dollar fuel safe-haven demand
item.description: Gold prices rose on Thursday as the ongoing military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran continued to drive investors toward safe-haven assets, while a retreat in the US dollar added further support to bullion.

item.title: Russian oil tankers reroute to India as Hormuz crisis chokes supply
item.description:
Two Russian oil tankers carrying a combined 1.4 million barrels of Urals crude have switched their destinations from East Asia to India, according to ship-tracking data from Kpler and Vortexa, as the escalating Middle East conflict forces New Delhi to revisit the Russian barrels it had been shunning under American pressure.

The Odune, a Suezmax carrying 730,000 barrels, arrived at the eastern port of Paradip on Wednesday, while the Matari, an Aframax with more than 700,000 barrels, is expected to reach Vadinar in western India on Thursday, Bloomberg reported. A third vessel, the Indri, made a sharp northward turn in the Arabian Sea this week toward India with another 730,000 barrels of Urals aboard. All three tankers were sanctioned by the United Kingdom and the European Union this year.

item.title: Alibaba forms AI task force after Qwen chief's abrupt exit
item.description:
Alibaba is setting up a new internal task force to accelerate its AI model development, a day after the abrupt resignation of Qwen technical lead Lin Junyang rattled investors and the open-source AI community.

CEO Eddie Wu will coordinate the task force alongside Alibaba Cloud CTO Zhou Jingren and Group CTO Wu Zeming, the company said Thursday in a staff letter that also confirmed Lin's departure and pledged to channel additional resources toward AI development. "In technology, standing still means falling behind," Wu wrote. "Advancing foundation models is a core strategic priority for our future."

item.title: Jet fuel hits record as Iran war chokes global supply
item.description:
Jet fuel prices in Singapore rocketed 72% to a record $225.44 a barrel on Wednesday, according to Reuters, underscoring how the war in Iran is rapidly translating into economic pain for energy consumers across Asia and beyond. The spot price of jet kerosene has now climbed 140% since February 27, the day before the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran in what has been dubbed "Operation Epic Fury".

The surge in aviation fuel — outpacing even the sharp rally in crude oil — reflects mounting fears about a prolonged disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption flows. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has declared "complete control" over the strait and warned that any vessel attempting to pass would be targeted.

item.title: Sri Lanka recovers 87 bodies from Iranian warship sunk by US submarine
item.description:
A U.S. Navy fast-attack submarine sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean on Tuesday with a single Mk-48 torpedo, marking the first time an American submarine has destroyed an enemy warship since 1945, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed at a Pentagon briefing Wednesday. Sri Lankan authorities said they recovered 87 bodies and rescued 32 survivors from the 180-member crew, with roughly 60 sailors still unaccounted for as search operations continued Thursday.

"Yesterday, in the Indian Ocean, an American submarine sunk an Iranian warship that thought it was safe in international waters," Hegseth told reporters. "Instead, it was sunk by a torpedo. Quiet death".

item.title: Bulk carrier signals 'China owner' to cross Hormuz blockade
item.description:
A bulk carrier signaled it was Chinese-owned as it transited the Strait of Hormuz early Thursday, underscoring how commercial vessels are improvising to ensure safe passage through the critical waterway as the war between Iran and a U.S.-Israeli coalition enters its second week.

The Iron Maiden changed its destination signal from "For Orders" to "CHINA OWNER" as it pushed through the passage while hugging the Omani coastline, according to ship-tracking data reported by Bloomberg and analytics firm Kpler. The vessel, which had been in the Persian Gulf since December delivering multiple shipments, is operated by Cetus Maritime Shanghai. A spokesperson for the company declined to comment, citing crew safety concerns.

item.title: Gold pulls back from record highs as Iran war enters second week
item.description: Gold prices surged to an all-time high above $5,400 per ounce this week as the escalating war between the United States, Israel, and Iran triggered a stampede into safe-haven assets. The precious metal has since pulled back from those peaks amid profit-taking, but remains elevated as the conflict enters its second week with no sign of resolution.

item.title: ECB warns Iran war's economic fallout poses risk to euro zone banks
item.description: Euro zone banks face only limited direct exposure to the war in Iran, but the broader European economy is at growing risk as rising energy prices and deepening uncertainty threaten to squeeze borrowers and reignite inflation, a senior European Central Bank supervisor warned on Wednesday.

item.title: European stocks slip as Iran conflict enters sixth day
item.description:
European equities fell on Thursday as a brief market rebound faded and the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its sixth day, renewing fears over energy supply disruptions and the broader economic fallout of the conflict.

The STOXX 50 dropped 0.6% and the STOXX 600 slipped 0.3% in early trading, erasing gains from Wednesday's relief rally. The pullback came as investors reassessed the likelihood of a prolonged conflict following Iran's claims of control over the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint that carries roughly one-fifth of the world's total oil consumption.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz nears full shutdown as Iran war enters second week
item.description: A U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, now entering its second week, has effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz and triggered the worst disruption to global energy markets in decades, compounding a supply squeeze that began when American forces toppled Venezuela's government in January.

item.title: U.S. submarine sinks Iranian warship, first torpedo strike since WWII
item.description:
A U.S. Navy fast attack submarine torpedoed and sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean on March 4, marking the first time an American submarine has sunk an enemy vessel in combat since World War II. Sri Lankan authorities said they recovered 87 bodies and rescued 32 survivors from a crew of approximately 180, with around 60 people still missing.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed the attack at a Pentagon briefing. "An American submarine sunk an Iranian warship that thought it was safe in international waters," Hegseth said. "Instead, it was sunk by a torpedo. Quiet death, the first sinking of an enemy ship by a torpedo since World War II. Like in that war, we are fighting to win."

item.title: Warwick and MIT upend catalyst science with new imaging breakthrough
item.description: Scientists at the University of Warwick and MIT have for the first time directly visualized how microscopic networks on catalyst surfaces coordinate chemical reactions, a finding that challenges long-held assumptions about how catalysts work and could accelerate the development of cleaner fuels and energy technologies.

item.title: US stock futures dip as Iran strikes oil tanker
item.description:
US stock futures edged lower Thursday morning as an escalating military conflict between the United States and Iran continued to unsettle investors, even as a batch of corporate earnings offered a mixed picture. S&P 500 futures slipped modestly in premarket trading, while Dow Jones futures also declined, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The pullback came after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that a US oil tanker had been struck by a missile in the northern Persian Gulf early Thursday, reigniting concerns about disruptions to global energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices pushed higher on the news, extending a rally that has persisted since US and Israeli forces launched strikes against Iran over the weekend.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine-Russia peace talks on hold amid Iran war
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced Wednesday evening that US-mediated peace negotiations with Russia have been put on hold indefinitely, as the escalating war in Iran consumes Washington's attention and has closed the airspace over the planned meeting venue in the United Arab Emirates.

"For now, because of the situation with Iran, the necessary signals for a trilateral meeting haven't come yet," Zelenskyy said in his nightly Telegram address to the nation. "But as soon as the security situation and the broader political context allow us to resume the trilateral diplomatic work, it will be done."

item.title: ECB, RBI brace for inflation as Iran war pushes oil past $83
item.description: The ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, now in its sixth day, is rippling through global financial markets and forcing central banks from Frankfurt to Mumbai to reassess their policy outlooks as surging energy prices threaten to reignite inflation.

item.title: Iranian drones strike Azerbaijan airport as war spreads to South Caucasus
item.description:
Drones launched from Iranian territory struck Azerbaijan's Nakhchivan International Airport on Thursday, damaging the terminal building and injuring two civilians, as the ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran threatened to draw the South Caucasus into a widening regional conflict.

Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry said the attack occurred around midday on March 5, with one drone hitting the airport terminal and a second crashing near a school in the village of Shakarabad. Baku summoned Iran's ambassador, Mojtaba Demirchilu, to deliver a formal protest and demanded Tehran provide "a clear explanation regarding the case" and take "urgent measures to ensure that such attacks are not repeated".

item.title: Iran war lifts Russia's oil revenue, but deep discounts limit the gains
item.description: The escalating conflict in the Middle East is delivering an unexpected financial lifeline to Moscow, as disruptions to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have pushed global crude prices sharply higher — boosting revenues for an energy-dependent economy that entered 2026 in dire fiscal straits. But analysts warn the rally may be too modest and too short-lived to rescue Russia's deteriorating budget.

item.title: Trump says he must help pick Iran's next leader
item.description:
President Donald Trump told Axios on Thursday that he needs to be directly involved in selecting Iran's next supreme leader, an extraordinary assertion of American influence over the internal succession of a sovereign nation now in the throes of a wartime leadership crisis.

"Khamenei's son is unacceptable to me. We want someone that will bring harmony and peace to Iran," Trump said in the interview, referring to Mojtaba Khamenei, son of the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. "I have to be involved in the appointment, like with Delcy in Venezuela," he added, drawing a direct parallel to the U.S.-backed removal of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro earlier this year.

Axios co-founder Jim VandeHei, who shared the exclusive, described Trump's stance as "Regime Change, Part 2," noting the president "will personally help pick the next leader of Iran" and called Khamenei's son "a weak, unacceptable option".

item.title: Scientists grow chickpeas in simulated moon dirt
item.description: As NASA prepares to return astronauts to the moon with the Artemis program, researchers at the University of Texas at Austin and Texas A&M University have answered a pressing question about what future lunar explorers might eat. The answer, according to a study published this week in the journal Scientific Reports, could be chickpeas.

item.title: Saudi Arabia triples Red Sea oil exports as Hormuz blockade fills Gulf storage
item.description:
Saudi Arabia is racing to divert millions of barrels of crude oil to its Red Sea port of Yanbu as the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran chokes off the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most critical oil shipping lane.

Five supertankers have already loaded at Yanbu in the first days of March, tripling the port's average February export volume, according to tanker-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. Aramco, the world's largest oil exporter, has informed buyers of its Arab Light crude that they must now load cargoes at the western port, according to Reuters.
